title: Robust, Clean and Shareable ML Code
oneLiner: Make ML code fail loudly and helpfully, read cleanly, and run the same on anyone's machine or as a service.

what.html:
Robust code catches bad input early and explains what went wrong. Clean code follows a consistent style, is checked by tools and is organised so it's easy to change. Shareable code lives in Git, pins its dependencies, can be installed as a package, runs in a container, and can be called by anyone through an API.

Everyday versionA good kitchen appliance refuses to start if the lid isn't on (fail fast), has a clear error light (logging), a manual anyone can follow (style), standard plugs (APIs) and works in any kitchen (Docker).

why.html:
• "If you don't build logging and error handling into your system, your users will become your loggers."
  • Notebooks that worked once often can't be rerun by anyone else.
  • A model nobody else can call or install creates no value.

how.title: Fail fast, fail clearly
how.html: Common ML errors: ValueError (wrong shapes), KeyError (missing column), TypeError (text where a number should be), IndexError. Catch the specific ones you expect, never a bare except:, and create your own like IncompatibleFeatureSizeError. Read tracebacks from the bottom up.

how.title: Log, don't print
how.html: Logs keep a timestamped, filterable history even after the terminal closes. Use DEBUG for detail, INFO for milestones, WARNING for odd-but-OK, ERROR for failures, CRITICAL when the system can't continue. Debug by explaining code to a rubber duck, shrinking the failing case, or using a debugger.

how.title: Style on autopilot
how.html: Follow PEP 8 (snake_case functions, PascalCase classes, 4-space indents, grouped imports). Let Black format, Ruff/Flake8/Pylint lint, and mypy check type hints like def scale(data: List[float], factor: float) -> List[float].

how.title: From notebook to production
how.html: Notebooks are for discovery; production needs modules, tests, config files and automation. Running cells out of order creates hidden state nobody can reproduce, so move proven code into .py files.

how.title: Refactor with SOLID
how.html: Refactoring improves structure without changing results. Spot smells: long functions, copy-paste, "god" classes, hard-coded paths. Fix them: extract functions, rename variables, name magic numbers, split into modules. SOLID: one job per function, extend without editing, depend on abstractions.

how.title: Serve the model through an API
how.html: Wrap the model in a web API: clients send JSON to /v1/predict and get a prediction back, from any language. FastAPI builds docs at /docs automatically, and Pydantic rejects bad input with an HTTP 422 error before the model sees it.

how.title: Share it properly
how.html: Use Git branches and pull requests; keep big data out of Git (use DVC). Pin dependencies in a virtual environment (requirements.txt, Conda or Poetry). Package shared code with pyproject.toml. Put everything in a Docker image so it runs the same everywhere.

demo.html: Type values into the request. Try age 150, income "lots" or a 2-character zip code and watch the API answer 422 with exactly what's wrong, without the model ever running.

example.html:
A churn model goes live. The notebook's cleaning, feature and training cells become data_loader.py, preprocessor.py, model_trainer.py and evaluator.py. Missing columns raise a clear KeyError message; a wrong feature count logs a WARNING and returns a documented default. Black, Ruff and mypy run on every commit. A FastAPI service validates requests with Pydantic, and the whole thing ships as a Docker image built from pinned requirements.

Supplementary Never log customers' personal data or API keys: logs are read by many people and kept for a long time.

misunderstandings: Catch every error with except: so the pipeline never crashes.
Bare except hides bugs and can trap interrupts; catch specific exceptions.
print() is as good as logging.
Logs persist, have levels and context, and can be searched centrally.
It changes structure, not behaviour; outputs should be identical.
Validate at the API boundary so bad input never reaches it.
takeaways: Fail fast with specific, meaningful (and custom) exceptions; read tracebacks bottom-up.
Use logging levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL) instead of print.
Automate style: PEP 8, Black, Ruff/Flake8/Pylint, mypy.
Production code: modules, tests, config, encapsulated state, CI/CD.
Serve models via FastAPI with Pydantic validation; share via Git, pinned dependencies, packages and Docker.
thirty: Robust ML code fails early and fast: common errors are ValueError, KeyError, TypeError and IndexError, and the code should catch specific exceptions with meaningful messages, never a bare except, and define custom exceptions for domain errors, reading tracebacks from the bottom up. Logging beats print through persistence, levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL) and metadata. Style is automated with PEP 8, Black, linters such as Ruff and type checking with mypy. Production code replaces notebooks' hidden state with modules, tests and configuration, and refactoring with SOLID principles, especially dependency inversion, keeps it flexible. Models are served through FastAPI endpoints whose Pydantic schemas return 422 for invalid input. Sharing relies on Git and DVC, virtual environments with pinned dependencies, pyproject.toml packages and Docker images.
